channel.description: Recent content in Sports on Trend Insights

item.title: Pat Summitt Documentary 'Breaking Glass' Premieres on Hulu During March Madness
item.description:
Pat Summitt won 1,098 games and never had a losing season in 38 years of coaching. Now, during the very tournament she helped make legendary, her full story is finally getting the documentary it deserves.

“Breaking Glass: The Pat Summitt Story” will premiere on Hulu on March 25 — right in the heart of Women’s March Madness. The timing is no accident. Few names in the history of women’s college basketball carry the weight that Summitt’s does, and this film aims to show the world why.

item.title: Carson Wentz Returns to Vikings: What It Means for Minnesota's Stacked QB Room
item.description:
What do you do when you already have two quarterbacks and sign a third? If you’re the Minnesota Vikings, you’re apparently building the most intriguing QB room in the NFL.

The Vikings announced on March 19 that they are re-signing Carson Wentz on a one-year free agent deal, reuniting with the veteran just months after trading for him before the 2025 season. This move comes on the heels of Minnesota’s blockbuster signing of Kyler Murray — making it three former first-round quarterbacks under one roof.

item.title: Vasco da Gama vs Fluminense: Essential Preview of Rio's Biggest Derby
item.description:
Twenty thousand tickets sold and counting — when Vasco da Gama and Fluminense meet at the Maracanã on March 19, 2026, it will be another chapter in one of the most passionate rivalries in South American football. After a dramatic 2025 that saw stoppage-time comebacks and decisive derby victories, this Brasileirão Serie A clash carries enormous weight for both clubs.

Key Takeaways:

  • Vasco da Gama vs Fluminense takes place at the Maracanã on March 19, 2026, in the Brasileirão Serie A.
  • Over 20,000 tickets have already been sold for the Rio clássico.
  • Vasco won both major meetings in 2025 — a 2-0 league win and a legendary 2-1 Copa do Brasil semi-final comeback in stoppage time.
  • Both teams deploy a 4-5-1 formation, setting up a tactical midfield battle.
  • Live broadcast available on ESPN and FOX Sports.

Recent History: Why This Derby Carries Extra Edge

Derbies need no additional motivation, but the recent history between these two sides makes this fixture especially charged. Vasco has dominated the head-to-head in the most recent meetings, and Fluminense will be desperate to reverse that trend.

item.title: Cameron Johnson's Surprising Rise Is Fueling the Nuggets' Playoff Push
item.description:
With about a month left in the NBA regular season, Cameron Johnson is finally starting to look like the player the Denver Nuggets envisioned when they acquired him. After battling injuries, adjusting to a new system, and admitting there is “still an element of figuring it out,” the veteran forward is stringing together his best stretch of basketball – and the timing could not be more important.

Quick Summary

  • Cameron Johnson has scored at least 15 points in three consecutive games, only the second time he has done that this season
  • He recently put up 18 points, 4 rebounds, 3 assists, a steal, and a block against the Lakers
  • Johnson has dealt with back spasms and an ankle injury, limiting his minutes in recent games
  • He is entering the final year of a $23.1 million contract and becomes extension-eligible this summer
  • The Denver Post called the Nuggets an “NBA Finals contender” when Johnson and Christian Braun find their groove

Cameron Johnson Admits He Is Still Adjusting to Denver

Honesty is refreshing in professional sports, and Johnson has been remarkably candid about his transition. Speaking to Bennett Durando of the Denver Post, the forward acknowledged that his first season with the Nuggets has required significant adjustment.

item.title: Cruz Azul Dominates CONCACAF Champions Cup With Stunning Comeback Victory
item.description:
When a team scores two goals in the final ten minutes to turn a deficit into a road victory, you know something special is unfolding. Cruz Azul did exactly that in the first leg of their 2026 CONCACAF Champions Cup Round of 16 series against CF Monterrey, and the reigning champions are showing no signs of slowing down.

Key Takeaways

  • Cruz Azul rallied from 2-1 down to win 3-2 away at Monterrey in the first leg
  • Gonzalo Piovi equalized via penalty in the 84th minute; Nicolas Ibanez scored the winner in the 90th
  • The second leg takes place at Estadio Cuauhtemoc in Puebla, Mexico
  • Cruz Azul also signed Argentine striker Nicolas Ibanez from Tigres ahead of the transfer deadline
  • The winner on aggregate advances to the CONCACAF Champions Cup Quarterfinals

Cruz Azul’s Dramatic First-Leg Comeback Against Monterrey

The first leg of this Round of 16 clash at Monterrey’s home ground looked like it was slipping away from La Maquina. Roberto de la Rosa scored both goals for Rayados, putting the hosts in a commanding 2-1 position deep into the second half.

item.title: Cade Cunningham Injury Update: What His Absence Means for the Surging Pistons
item.description:
Cade Cunningham will not suit up Tuesday night against the Washington Wizards, and for a Detroit Pistons franchise riding the highest wave in over a decade, the timing raises real questions about whether their MVP candidate can stay healthy through the postseason push.

Key Takeaway:

  • Cade Cunningham is out Tuesday vs. the Wizards due to an ongoing hip injury
  • He has already missed 3 games this season, also dealing with a left quadriceps issue
  • The Pistons are 13-2 and first in the Eastern Conference, holding a three-game lead over the Cleveland Cavaliers
  • Detroit rode an 11-game winning streak to the top of the standings
  • Cunningham is averaging a career-best 27.3 points per game with 9.9 assists (second in the NBA)
  • At just 24 years old, he recently signed a signature shoe deal with Nike — one of only 6 active NBA players with that distinction

The Rise Nobody Predicted

Two years ago, the Detroit Pistons were the laughingstock of the NBA. Endless losing, revolving-door coaching, and a fanbase that had largely checked out. The idea that Cade Cunningham — the former number one overall pick — would be leading this franchise to first place in the Eastern Conference felt like pure fantasy.

item.title: DJ Wonnum Signs With Detroit Lions: Why This $6 Million Bet Could Transform Their Pass Rush
item.description:
The Detroit Lions just made one of the quieter but most strategically important moves of free agency so far — signing edge rusher DJ Wonnum to a one-year deal worth up to $6 million. In a league where elite pass rushers command $25 million annually, this looks like a bargain. But is it a steal or a gamble?

Key Takeaway:

  • DJ Wonnum signed a one-year deal worth up to $6 million with the Detroit Lions, confirmed by ESPN’s Adam Schefter
  • The 28-year-old brings 30 career sacks across 6 NFL seasons, including two 8-sack campaigns
  • Detroit desperately needed edge depth behind star Aidan Hutchinson, who had only Ahmed Hassanein and Tyler Lacy behind him on the roster
  • Wonnum was a fourth-round pick out of South Carolina by the Minnesota Vikings in 2020
  • His 2025 season with Carolina produced 42 total tackles, 3 sacks, and 1 interception in 16 games with 15 starts
  • The Panthers ranked near the bottom of the NFL in sacks and quarterback pressures last season

From Viking to Panther to Lion: Wonnum’s Journey to Detroit

DJ Wonnum’s career arc tells the story of a player who has always shown flashes of dominance without fully breaking through to stardom. Selected in the fourth round of the 2020 NFL Draft by the Minnesota Vikings, Wonnum immediately proved he belonged in the league. His initial rookie contract was a modest four-year, $4.04 million deal — a fraction of what first-rounders command.

item.title: Jaylen Waddle Trade: Dolphins Ship Star WR to Broncos in Blockbuster Deal
item.description:
The NFL offseason just delivered its biggest headline yet. The Miami Dolphins are trading wide receiver Jaylen Waddle to the Denver Broncos, a blockbuster move reported simultaneously by NFL Network’s Tom Pelissero and ESPN’s Adam Schefter. This deal reshapes two franchises going in completely opposite directions — and it’s exactly the kind of seismic transaction that makes March the most chaotic month in professional football.

Key Takeaways: The Dolphins are trading Jaylen Waddle — a three-time 1,000-yard receiver — to the Broncos along with a 4th-round pick. Denver sends back a 1st-rounder (30th overall), a late 3rd, and a late 4th. Miami is in full rebuild mode. Denver is going all-in on Bo Nix.

item.title: Waddle to Denver: How One Trade Could Fuel the Broncos' Super Bowl Pursuit
item.description: The Denver Broncos have a problem — or rather, they had one. After falling agonizingly short of the Super Bowl last season, the question hanging over their entire offseason was simple: are they actually close enough, or did they just get lucky? The acquisition of Jaylen Waddle from the Miami Dolphins answers that question loudly and clearly. Denver’s front office believes this team is a weapon away from a championship run, and they’ve just found that weapon.

item.title: Broncos Depth Chart 2026: Blockbuster Trade and Free Agency Reshape Denver's Roster
item.description:
The Denver Broncos are not the same team they were two weeks ago. After a blockbuster trade for a star wide receiver and an aggressive first wave of NFL free agency, the Broncos depth chart has undergone a transformation that signals one thing clearly: Denver is done waiting and ready to compete right now.

Key Takeaway:

  • The Broncos completed a blockbuster trade for a star wide receiver on March 17, dramatically upgrading their passing attack
  • Denver’s first wave of free agency brought significant roster changes across multiple position groups
  • Running back J.K. Dobbins was re-signed, solidifying the backfield alongside RJ Harvey
  • The 2025 season exposed serious depth issues at wide receiver after injuries to Troy Franklin and Pat Bryant
  • Denver’s projected depth chart for 2026 reflects a franchise shifting from rebuild to contention mode

A Blockbuster Trade Changes Everything

The biggest headline rocking the Broncos depth chart came on March 17, when Denver completed a blockbuster trade to acquire a star wide receiver. The move was reported by Broncos Wire and immediately reshuffled the entire offensive pecking order in Denver.

item.title: Tyreek Hill Free Agency: Where Will the Cheetah Land After Dolphins Release?
item.description: For the first time in his NFL career, Tyreek Hill is an unrestricted free agent — and the circumstances surrounding his availability are unlike anything the league has seen from a receiver of his caliber. The eight-time Pro Bowler and five-time All-Pro wasn’t cut because he lost a step. He was released because a devastating knee injury, a $51.1 million cap hit, and a franchise-wide rebuild in Miami collided all at once.

item.title: David Ortiz WBC 2026: Big Papi Steals the Show as Broadcaster and Red Sox Mentor
item.description: David Ortiz hasn’t swung a bat in a major league game since 2016, but somehow Big Papi is still the biggest personality in baseball. At the 2026 World Baseball Classic in Miami, the Hall of Famer has been everywhere — breaking down games on the FOX Sports desk, embracing young stars, and doing what he’s always done best: making everyone around him feel like they belong on the biggest stage.

item.title: Kevin Durant MVP Push: Rockets Star Dominates at 37 With Historic Scoring Streak
item.description: At 37 years old, most NBA players are winding down their careers, accepting reduced roles, and mentoring younger teammates from the bench. Kevin Durant didn’t get that memo. The Houston Rockets forward is in the middle of one of the most remarkable late-career surges in league history, climbing into the top 10 of the MVP ladder and reminding everyone why he’s considered one of the greatest scorers to ever touch a basketball.

item.title: Mavericks vs Pelicans: Surprising Southwest Division Battle With Playoff Elimination Stakes
item.description:
The Dallas Mavericks have gone 4-19 over the last two months. The New Orleans Pelicans have gone 9-6 in their last 15 games. When these two Southwest Division rivals met at the Smoothie King Center on March 16, the contrast could not have been sharper — and neither could the stakes.

Key Takeaways

  • Dallas (23-45) entered on a 4-19 stretch over two months after officially embracing a tank strategy.
  • New Orleans (22-46) was riding its best stretch of basketball all season, going 9-6 in the last 15 games.
  • Cooper Flagg scored 27 points with 10 assists in Dallas’s shocking 130-120 upset of Cleveland the night before.
  • Dejounte Murray was listed as questionable due to illness after dropping a season-high 35 points against Houston.
  • Klay Thompson was downgraded to OUT, resting on the second night of a back-to-back.
  • The Pelicans led the season series 2-1 heading into this fourth and final meeting.

Mavericks vs Pelicans: A Tale of Two Trajectories

On paper, these teams look nearly identical. Dallas sat at 23-45, New Orleans at 22-46 — separated by just a single game near the bottom of the Western Conference. But the trajectories heading into Monday night told a completely different story.

item.title: Grizzlies vs Bulls: Essential Breakdown of a Pivotal Lottery Showdown
item.description:
When the Memphis Grizzlies rolled into the United Center to face the Chicago Bulls on March 16, neither team was playing for playoff glory. They were playing for something arguably just as valuable — lottery positioning.

Key Takeaways

  • Memphis (23-43) entered riding a brutal seven-game losing streak, the longest of their season.
  • Chicago (27-40) went winless in February and traded key role players at the deadline.
  • Only 3.5 games separated these two teams in the tank race, making every outcome critical for draft lottery odds.
  • Josh Giddey recorded three triple-doubles in his last four games, while Matas Buzelis scored 20+ points in six of his last eight contests.
  • Memphis listed six players as out with additional doubtful and questionable designations.

Grizzlies vs Bulls: Two Franchises at a Crossroads

This was the first meeting between the Grizzlies and Bulls all season, and the circumstances could not have been more dramatic. Memphis came in with the eighth-worst record in the league at 23-43, while Chicago sat at 27-40 — close enough to make every game a swing in the draft lottery calculus.

item.title: Talia Gibson's Stunning Indian Wells Run: From Qualifier to Quarter-Finalist
item.description:
She walked into Indian Wells ranked No. 112 in the world, without even a profile picture on the official WTA website. She walked out as one of the biggest stories in tennis. Talia Gibson, a 21-year-old from Perth, Australia, has turned the 2026 BNP Paribas Open into her own fairy tale — and the tennis world is still catching its breath.

Key Takeaways

  • Talia Gibson entered Indian Wells ranked No. 112 and rose to No. 67 in the live WTA rankings.
  • She was 0-9 against Top 50 players before the tournament, then won four consecutive Top 50 matches.
  • Her victory over No. 7 seed Jasmine Paolini (7-5, 2-6, 6-1) was her first-ever Top 10 match and win.
  • Gibson is the first women’s qualifier to reach the Indian Wells quarterfinals since Lesia Tsurenko in 2015.
  • She guaranteed herself $270,000 in prize money — nearly matching her entire prior career earnings of $325,000.
  • Gibson has been selected for Australia’s Billie Jean King Cup squad.

Talia Gibson’s Path Through the Draw: Upset After Upset

Gibson’s run at Indian Wells was not a single lucky win. It was a sustained demolition of some of the best players on tour, all accomplished by a player who had to qualify just to enter the main draw.

item.title: Thad Matta Retires: The End of a Remarkable 502-Win Coaching Career at Butler
item.description:
Just days after Butler’s athletic director publicly stated that Thad Matta would return for another season, the longtime college basketball coach reversed course and announced his retirement on Monday. With 502 career wins across 21 seasons, Matta leaves the sidelines as one of the most accomplished coaches of his generation — but he is not leaving Butler entirely.

Key Takeaways

  • Thad Matta retires with a 502-223 career record spanning 21 seasons at Butler, Xavier, and Ohio State.
  • He will remain at Butler as Special Assistant to the President and Athletic Director.
  • Matta made 13 NCAA Tournament appearances, including two Final Fours and one national championship game.
  • Butler has begun a national search for a new head coach.
  • The retirement comes after a 16-16 overall and 7-13 Big East season for the Bulldogs.

Thad Matta’s Sudden Retirement Announcement

The timing caught many off guard. On Friday, March 13, Butler Athletic Director Grant Leiendecker tried to dispel swirling rumors about Matta’s future, publicly stating the coach would return for another year. The Butler Collegian even reported that Matta was set to come back.

item.title: Gavi's Comeback: Barcelona Star Returns After Seven-Month Injury Absence
item.description:
Seven months without one of the most talented young midfielders in world football. For Barcelona, the wait is finally over.

Quick Summary: Gavi has received medical clearance to return for Barcelona’s La Liga match against Sevilla, ending a seven-month injury absence. Head coach Hansi Flick has described himself as “really happy” about the midfielder’s return, calling it a major boost for their title challenge. The Pedri-Gavi reunion in Barcelona’s midfield is one of the most anticipated storylines in La Liga this season.

item.title: Tyler Tanner's Record-Breaking Run: How Vanderbilt Stormed the SEC Tournament
item.description:
A program that was once an afterthought in the SEC just knocked off the conference’s top seed. And a record-breaking defensive performance was at the heart of it all.

Quick Summary: Vanderbilt’s Tyler Tanner delivered a historic defensive performance as the Commodores took down top-seeded Florida 91-74 to reach the SEC Tournament final. This followed a 75-68 upset over Tennessee in the quarterfinals. Tanner’s back-to-back performances have been described as record-breaking, putting Vanderbilt in position for a deep March Madness run.

item.title: Derrick Jones Jr.'s Essential Role in the Clippers' 2026 Playoff Push
item.description:
A player once known primarily for slam dunk contests is quietly producing top-20 fantasy value and anchoring the Clippers’ defense during their playoff chase.

Quick Summary: Derrick Jones Jr. has emerged as the LA Clippers’ X-factor in their 2026 playoff push. He’s scored in double digits in 8 of his last 9 games, recorded 15 combined steals and blocks in 3 games, and has been described as delivering “elite two-way production.” However, recent injuries — including a head injury against the Knicks and a knee collision — have raised concerns about his availability down the stretch.

item.title: Celtic vs Motherwell: Scottish Premiership Title Race Heats Up in Crucial Clash
item.description:
Can Celtic afford another slip-up? With nine games left and a five-point deficit to league leaders Hearts, every match is now a must-win for the Bhoys.

Quick Summary: Celtic host Motherwell at Celtic Park in a Scottish Premiership clash with major title implications. Martin O’Neill’s side sit second, five points behind Hearts, while Motherwell — managed by Celtic-linked Jens Berthel Askou — are fourth, 10 points off the pace. Celtic are unbeaten in eight of their last nine league games under O’Neill’s second interim spell, but Motherwell already beat them 2-0 in December.

item.title: Jeremy Fears Jr. All-American: Michigan State's Record-Chasing Point Guard
item.description:
Jeremy Fears Jr. is 27 assists away from rewriting Michigan State basketball history. The redshirt sophomore point guard has turned a season that began with questions into one that has produced All-American recognition, a Big Ten First Team selection, and a legitimate shot at breaking Cassius Winston’s single-season assist record – one of the most revered marks in Spartan lore.

At 15.5 points and 9.1 assists per game, Fears has established himself as one of the most productive floor generals in all of college basketball. His 264 assists on the season lead the Big Ten, and the record of 291 set by Winston – now an NBA veteran – is firmly within reach.

item.title: Randy Orton Turns Heel: Viper Bloodies Cody Rhodes in Shocking WrestleMania 42 Contract Signing
item.description:
There is something uniquely chilling about watching a friendship die on live television. On the March 13 episode of WWE SmackDown, Randy Orton did exactly what millions of fans feared and many more secretly hoped for – he turned on Cody Rhodes during the WrestleMania 42 contract signing, leaving the American Nightmare bloodied in the ring.

The attack was sudden, methodical, and unmistakably Orton at his most dangerous. Just like that, the Viper shed his skin and reminded the wrestling world why he has been one of the most feared competitors in WWE history for over two decades.

item.title: Ohio State vs Michigan Basketball: Can the 8th-Seed Buckeyes Shock the Big Ten's Best?
item.description:
The stage is set for one of college basketball’s fiercest rivalries to take center court in Chicago. Ohio State, the 8th seed, will square off against top-seeded Michigan in the Big Ten Tournament quarterfinals on March 13, 2026, at the United Center, with tipoff scheduled for noon ET on Big Ten Network.

Michigan enters with a staggering 29-2 record and a 19-1 mark in Big Ten play, while Ohio State (21-11) had to claw past Iowa just to earn this matchup. The question everyone is asking: does Ohio State have any realistic path to an upset, or is Michigan simply too dominant?

item.title: Spencer Jones Optioned: Why the Yankees' Top Prospect Is Headed to Triple-A
item.description:
Spencer Jones homered. Spencer Jones impressed. And then Spencer Jones was sent to minor league camp anyway. The New York Yankees’ decision to option one of their most exciting young talents to Triple-A, despite a standout spring training performance, has become one of the most talked-about storylines heading into the 2026 MLB season.

Key Takeaways:

  • Spencer Jones was reassigned to minor league camp on Monday, March 9
  • Jones homered alongside Jasson Dominguez in a Yankees win over the Phillies on March 10
  • The Yankees’ deep outfield roster left no room for Jones on the Opening Day squad
  • Jones has drawn comparisons to Shohei Ohtani for his blend of size, power, and athleticism
  • Both Jones and Jasson Dominguez are expected to begin the season in the minors

A Spring to Remember, Then a Trip Down

Spencer Jones turned heads throughout spring training in 2026. The towering outfield prospect showcased the raw power and athleticism that made him one of the Yankees’ most coveted young players, and he punctuated his Grapefruit League stint with a home run in a Yankees victory over the Philadelphia Phillies at Clearwater on March 10.

item.title: Utah Mammoth Lock In Nick Schmaltz with Massive $64 Million Extension
item.description:
The Utah Mammoth just made one of the biggest moves of the NHL season, and it signals exactly where this franchise is headed. By locking in Nick Schmaltz to an eight-year, $64 million contract extension, the Mammoth have removed one of the league’s top pending free agents from the open market and planted a flag for long-term competitiveness in Salt Lake City.

Key Takeaways:

  • Nick Schmaltz signs an 8-year extension worth $64 million ($8 million AAV)
  • The Mammoth hold 73 points through 65 games in their second season since relocating from Arizona
  • GM Bill Armstrong continues an aggressive roster-building approach
  • Utah plans to be aggressive in the summer trade market, particularly targeting centers
  • Defenseman Mikhail Sergachev returns to the lineup after missing over a week

The Schmaltz Deal: Breaking Down the Numbers

The contract, announced on Wednesday, March 11, carries a cap hit of $8.0 million per season over eight years. For a forward who was set to become an unrestricted free agent this summer, the deal represents a significant commitment from both sides.

item.title: Jaquan Brisker Free Agency: Where Will the Former Bears Safety Land?
item.description:
Jaquan Brisker Remains One of the Best Players Still Available in Free Agency

The first wave of 2026 NFL free agency has come and gone, and one name keeps surfacing in trade rumors and landing-spot speculation: Jaquan Brisker. The hard-hitting safety spent the first four years of his career with the Chicago Bears, but the relationship appears to be over. With the Bears pivoting to other options and multiple contenders circling, Brisker’s next move could reshape a secondary across the league.

item.title: Jacob Martin Signs with Titans: $11M Deal Reunites Edge Rusher with Robert Saleh
item.description:
Jacob Martin Cashes In: Titans Land Edge Rusher on Two-Year Deal

The Tennessee Titans continue their aggressive 2026 free agency spending spree. On March 12, the team agreed to sign outside linebacker Jacob Martin to a two-year deal worth up to $11 million, according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz.

The signing reunites Martin with Titans head coach Robert Saleh, who previously coached him during their time together with the New York Jets in 2022.

item.title: Kawhi Leonard Fuels Clippers' Stunning Turnaround After Disastrous Start
item.description:
Few players in NBA history have carried a team from the edge of irrelevance back into the playoff picture the way Kawhi Leonard is doing right now. After the LA Clippers lost 21 of their first 27 games this season, most analysts had already written their obituary. Leonard had other plans.

Key Takeaways

  • Kawhi Leonard is averaging 28.0 points, 6.4 rebounds, 3.7 assists, and 2.0 steals per game on elite shooting splits
  • The Clippers clawed back from a 6-21 start to reach .500 at 32-32, surpassing the Warriors for 8th in the Western Conference
  • An NBA investigation into a $28 million endorsement deal with Aspiration has raised salary cap circumvention questions
  • Despite the turnaround, Leonard insists there is “nothing to be happy about” — the job is far from finished

Kawhi Leonard’s Monster Season by the Numbers

Leonard’s individual performance this season has been nothing short of extraordinary. At 34 years old, the two-time Finals MVP is putting up numbers that rival his peak seasons in San Antonio and Toronto.

item.title: Knicks vs Jazz Breakdown: Karl-Anthony Towns Dominates as New York Eyes Eastern Conference Surge
item.description:
Nobody in the NBA is collecting double-doubles faster than Karl-Anthony Towns right now, and the Utah Jazz are about to find out why.

The New York Knicks enter their March 11 matchup against the Utah Jazz riding a wave of momentum as one of the most dangerous teams in the Eastern Conference. At 41-25, they sit firmly in third place, while Utah limps into Madison Square Garden with a brutal 20-45 record near the bottom of the Western Conference. The last time these two teams met? The Knicks obliterated them 146-112 in December.

item.title: WVU Basketball Big 12 Tournament: Mountaineers' NCAA Hopes on the Line
item.description:
WVU basketball needs a miracle run — and they know it. The seventh-seeded West Virginia Mountaineers enter the Big 12 Tournament at 18-13, sitting firmly on the outside of the NCAA Tournament bubble. Their only path to March Madness likely runs through Kansas City.

Key Takeaways

  • WVU enters the Big 12 Tournament as the 7th seed with an 18-13 record
  • The Mountaineers are off Joe Lunardi’s NCAA Tournament bubble
  • Key wins this season: Kansas, BYU, and Pitt (71-49)
  • Senior guard Honor Huff earned All-Big 12 Honorable Mention
  • WVU women’s basketball won the Big 12 title and may host NCAA games

WVU Basketball’s Roller-Coaster Season Under Ross Hodge

First-year head coach Ross Hodge has navigated a season full of extremes. The highs have been exhilarating — none more than a 71-49 demolition of rival Pitt that Hodge says he’ll “never forget for as long as I live.”

item.title: Kai Havertz Haunts Former Club: Arsenal's Penalty Hero Secures 1-1 Draw at Leverkusen
item.description:
Kai Havertz stepped up when it mattered most. Returning to the BayArena where his career began, the 26-year-old Arsenal forward converted a late penalty to secure a crucial 1-1 draw against Bayer Leverkusen in the Champions League Round of 16 first leg.

Key Takeaways

  • Bayer Leverkusen 1-1 Arsenal — Kai Havertz scored a late penalty to level for the Gunners
  • Robert Andrich headed Leverkusen ahead from a corner kick
  • Noni Madueke won the penalty after being fouled by Malik Tillman in the 87th minute
  • Havertz made just his 10th appearance of the season after two surgeries in seven months
  • Arsenal won all 8 league phase matches — the only team with a perfect record

Havertz’s Remarkable Comeback — From “Worst Pain” to Match Hero

The story of Kai Havertz’s 2025-26 season reads more like a medical drama than a football highlight reel. According to BBC Sport, ESPN, and Sky Sports, the German international has endured a nightmare stretch of injuries:

item.title: Trey Hendrickson Injury Update: How a Core Muscle Surgery Is Reshaping NFL Free Agency
item.description:
The most dominant pass rusher of the last three NFL seasons is sitting at home without a team, and a single surgery is the reason why.

Trey Hendrickson, the four-time Pro Bowl defensive end, entered 2026 free agency expecting a bidding war. Instead, he got silence, lowball offers, and a gap between his asking price and reality that could be as wide as $10 million per year. The culprit? A core muscle injury that cut his 2025 season to just seven games and forced him under the knife in December.
